summary: The computer component is the loop's desktop-automation hand: MouseController (move, click, drag, scroll with Linear/EaseInOut/Bezier profiles), KeyboardController (type, key combos with a TypingProfile), ScreenCapture (CapturedScreen over a ScreenRegion), and WindowManager (WindowInfo/WindowId, display-server aware). Every action passes an ActionRateLimiter (default 10/sec) and a BLOCKED_COMBOS safety list, and first use per session needs confirmation. On the loop it is the archetypal act stage for GUI targets — it emits PointerEvents and KeyEvents into the OS — but its screen capture is also a raw perceive source. On a touch canvas its objects map one-to-one to real gestures: a loop-node's click becomes your tap, its drag becomes your drag, its pinch becomes a scroll.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with computer read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where every action is rate-limited, dangerous combos are blocked, first use needs confirmation, and all actions log to the audit trail.

examples.title: Capture the screen as a perceive source
examples.intent: Feed the loop a visual snapshot of the desktop before acting.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ScreenCapture produces a CapturedScreen the loop reads to ground its next act; it adds a perceive step but no OS mutation, so it is safe and idempotent.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the screen node grabs a fresh CapturedScreen and shows it as a thumbnail on the node.
touch_interaction.visual: The node fills with the live capture; a shutter flash animates on grab.

examples.mini_scenario: Before clicking a button the loop captures the screen, locating the button's Point from the image.
examples.pitfall: A stale capture leads to clicking the wrong Point — re-capture after any UI change.

examples.title: Scope capture to a ScreenRegion
examples.intent: Grab only the region that matters to cut noise and tokens.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A ScreenRegion (x,y,w,h) narrows the CapturedScreen so the perceive payload is smaller, keeping the loop's context budget lean.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading two fingers on the screen node draws a rectangle that becomes the ScreenRegion.
touch_interaction.visual: A selection rectangle rubber-bands out; the captured region renders inside it, the rest dimmed.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop captures just the dialog region to read its text without the whole 4K desktop.
examples.pitfall: A region outside screen bounds returns nothing — clamp the rectangle to the display.

examples.title: Move the pointer to a target Point
examples.intent: Place the cursor precisely before a click.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MouseController moves to a Point using a MovementProfile; it is the act primitive that positions the loop's hand, one PointerEvent that the rate limiter counts.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the pointer node to a coordinate sets the target Point for the next move.
touch_interaction.visual: A crosshair glides to the point along the chosen profile's curve; Bezier shows a natural arc.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop moves to (640,480) with a Bezier profile to look human before clicking submit.
examples.pitfall: Linear moves are instant and machine-obvious — for anti-bot targets prefer EaseInOut/Bezier.

examples.title: Click with a chosen MouseButton
examples.intent: Trigger a UI element with the correct button.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A click emits a PointerEvent for Left/Right/Middle; it advances the loop from a positioned state to an interaction, counted by the ActionRateLimiter.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the click node fires the configured button at the current Point.
touch_interaction.visual: A ripple radiates from the point; the button badge (L/R/M) flashes on the node.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop left-clicks the 'Save' button, then captures the screen to verify the save dialog closed.
examples.pitfall: Right-click opens a context menu, not an activation — pick the button the target actually expects.

examples.title: Drag from one Point to another
examples.intent: Move a slider, node, or file by dragging.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A drag issues press-move-release PointerEvents between two Points; it is a compound act the loop treats atomically, still bounded by the rate limiter.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging between two anchors on the pointer node defines the drag's from→to Points.
touch_interaction.visual: A dashed path connects the anchors; a ghost cursor traces it on preview.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop drags a canvas node from (100,100) to (400,300) to reposition it in the target app.
examples.pitfall: A drag that crosses a drop-forbidden zone silently no-ops in some apps — verify the drop landed.

examples.title: Scroll to bring a target into view
examples.intent: Expose an off-screen element before interacting.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A scroll PointerEvent shifts the viewport so a later act has its target visible; it is a preparatory act that changes perceive state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking on the scroll node emits scroll ticks in the flick direction.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shows a scrollbar thumb sliding; momentum decays like a real flick.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop scrolls a long form down until the submit button enters the captured region.
examples.pitfall: Scroll amount is app-relative — re-capture and confirm the target is visible rather than assuming.

examples.title: Type text with a TypingProfile
examples.intent: Enter text into a focused field.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: KeyboardController emits a KeyEvent per character with base_delay/variation from the TypingProfile; the act's cadence is tunable and each keystroke counts against the rate limiter.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the keyboard node with text bound streams KeyEvents into the focused target.
touch_interaction.visual: Characters appear one by one on the node with a per-key tick; jitter reflects the variation setting.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop types a search query with a 40ms±15ms profile so input looks human.
examples.pitfall: Type only into a confirmed-focused field — an unfocused type scatters keys or triggers shortcuts.

examples.title: Send a safe key combo
examples.intent: Invoke a keyboard shortcut like Ctrl+S.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A combo KeyEvent triggers app actions in one act; the loop reaches a result faster than mouse navigation, subject to the blocked-combo guard.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the combo node fires the bound key combination.
touch_interaction.visual: The key caps light up together and flash; a chord glyph confirms the combo.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop sends Ctrl+S to save, then captures to confirm the modified indicator cleared.
examples.pitfall: Combos are app-focus sensitive — sending Ctrl+S to the wrong window saves the wrong thing.

examples.title: Block a dangerous combo before it fires
examples.intent: Refuse destructive system key combinations.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_blocked_combo checks against BLOCKED_COMBOS (ctrl+alt+delete, cmd+q, alt+f4, TTY switches); a blocked combo aborts the act and routes the loop back to reason.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a blocked combo node shakes it and refuses to fire.
touch_interaction.visual: The combo node turns red with a 🚫 overlay; the keystroke never leaves the node.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop tries alt+f4 to close a window; is_blocked_combo rejects it, so the window stays open.
examples.pitfall: Normalization lowercases and strips spaces — a combo formatted oddly must still match the blocklist.

examples.title: Throttle actions through the rate limiter
examples.intent: Cap action frequency to stay human-plausible and safe.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ActionRateLimiter.check() enforces max 10 actions/sec in a sliding window; when exceeded, the act must wait, pacing the loop's hand like a budget guard on iteration speed.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the rate-limiter node shows the current window count and remaining budget.
touch_interaction.visual: A per-second gauge fills; when full the gauge reddens and queued acts stack.

examples.mini_scenario: A burst of 15 clicks in one second hits the limit; the 11th onward wait for the next window.
examples.pitfall: The window uses saturating_sub to survive clock skew — don't replace it with plain subtraction.

examples.title: Enumerate windows with WindowManager
examples.intent: Discover available windows before choosing one to act on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WindowManager lists WindowInfo (with WindowId) so the loop perceives the desktop topology and picks a target, without mutating anything.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch-out on the window node fans the open windows into a grid of WindowInfo cards.
touch_interaction.visual: Each card shows a title and WindowId; the focused window is ringed.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop lists windows, finds the 'Terminal' WindowInfo, and targets its WindowId next.
examples.pitfall: Window lists change constantly — resolve the WindowId immediately before acting, not from a stale list.

examples.title: Focus a window before interacting
examples.intent: Ensure input goes to the intended window.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Raising/focusing a WindowId directs subsequent KeyEvents/PointerEvents there; it is a control-of-target act that scopes where the loop's hand lands.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a WindowInfo card raises and focuses that window.
touch_interaction.visual: The tapped card lifts to the front with a focus glow; others recede.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop focuses the editor window, then types — guaranteeing keys land in the editor.
examples.pitfall: Focus can be stolen by popups between focus and type — re-verify focus for critical input.

examples.title: Detect the display server for capability
examples.intent: Know whether automation is supported on this platform.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WindowManager.detect()/display_server()/is_supported() tell the loop if it can act at all (X11/Wayland/WSL/macOS limits), gating the whole computer act family.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the computer node reveals the detected backend and support status.
touch_interaction.visual: A capability badge shows xdotool/WSL/unsupported; unsupported greys out the act nodes.

examples.mini_scenario: On macOS the loop detects mouse acts are unsupported and returns an explicit error instead of a silent no-op.
examples.pitfall: macOS mouse control errors explicitly by design — treat 'not supported' as a real failure, not success.

examples.title: Confirm first computer use per session
examples.intent: Require explicit approval before the loop touches the desktop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: First-use-per-session confirmation inserts a control checkpoint before any act, so the loop cannot silently seize the mouse/keyboard.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the first act raises a consent sheet the operator must approve.
touch_interaction.visual: A shield overlay pulses; act nodes stay locked until the operator confirms.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop's first click of the session pauses for a 'allow desktop control?' confirmation.
examples.pitfall: Don't cache consent across sessions — the gate is per-session on purpose.

examples.title: Audit every action to the trail
examples.intent: Record what the loop did on the desktop for review.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each mouse/keyboard act logs to the audit trail, giving the learn stage a durable record of PointerEvents/KeyEvents the loop emitted.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking down the computer node scrolls the audit log of recent actions.
touch_interaction.visual: A ledger panel lists timestamped click/type events with their targets.

examples.mini_scenario: After a run the operator scrolls the audit to confirm the loop only clicked the intended buttons.
examples.pitfall: Never suppress the audit for 'noisy' actions — the full trail is the safety record.

examples.title: Choose a movement profile for realism
examples.intent: Pick how human the pointer path should look.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Selecting Linear/EaseInOut/Bezier as the MovementProfile shapes the act's kinematics; the reason stage trades speed for plausibility.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating a dial on the pointer node cycles Linear → EaseInOut → Bezier.
touch_interaction.visual: A preview trail redraws per profile: a straight line, a smooth ease, or a natural arc.

examples.mini_scenario: For a captcha-guarded page the loop selects Bezier so the cursor path isn't robotically straight.
examples.pitfall: Bezier adds randomness — for pixel-exact targets confirm the final Point still lands dead-on.

examples.title: Verify an act by re-capturing
examples.intent: Confirm the UI changed as expected after an action.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After a click/type the loop captures a new CapturedScreen and compares, closing the perceive→act→verify cycle for GUI work.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the verify node overlays before/after captures for a visual diff.
touch_interaction.visual: Changed pixels highlight; an unchanged region flags the act as possibly ineffective.

examples.mini_scenario: After clicking submit the loop re-captures and confirms a success toast appeared.
examples.pitfall: Compare a stable region — animations cause false diffs that look like the act failed.

examples.title: Fall back across backends safely
examples.intent: Keep automation working when xdotool is absent.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The mouse backend detects xdotool, else WSL PowerShell, else none — the loop's act layer adapts to the host without changing higher-stage logic.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the pointer node shows which backend is driving the acts.
touch_interaction.visual: A backend badge (xdotool / WSL) pins to the node; 'none' locks it red.

examples.mini_scenario: Under WSL2 without xdotool the loop routes clicks through PowerShell's mouse_event fallback.
examples.pitfall: Backends differ subtly in coordinate origins — re-validate Points when the backend changes.

examples.title: Read a WindowInfo geometry to aim
examples.intent: Translate a window-relative target into absolute Points.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WindowInfo geometry lets the loop compute absolute Points from window-relative positions, grounding the act's coordinates in perceive data.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch-in on a WindowInfo card zooms to its bounds with a coordinate grid.
touch_interaction.visual: The window's frame renders with x/y/w/h labels; a tapped spot shows its absolute Point.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop reads the editor window's origin and adds a relative offset to click a menu inside it.
examples.pitfall: Window moves invalidate cached geometry — recompute Points after any focus or resize.

examples.title: Compose a GUI macro on the canvas
examples.intent: Wire a repeatable capture→move→click→type sequence.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Chaining computer acts under one control node builds a macro the loop replays; each link is a rate-limited, audited act, forming a deterministic sub-loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing edges between capture, move, click, and type nodes composes them into an ordered macro.
touch_interaction.visual: A pulsing pipeline animates the sequence order; each node lights as it executes.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop wires capture→locate button→move→click→verify into a login macro it runs each session.
examples.pitfall: Between macro steps the UI can shift — insert re-capture/verify links rather than trusting fixed Points.
